title: Auto Scaling groups: elasticity for EC2

kcs.statement: An Auto Scaling group keeps its number of EC2 instances between a set minimum and maximum, starting at a desired capacity, and replaces instances that fail health checks.
Auto Scaling provides elasticity: it adds instances when demand rises and removes them when demand falls, so you pay only for the capacity the load needs.

Target tracking scaling holds a metric such as 50% average CPU. Step scaling reacts to alarm thresholds. Scheduled scaling changes capacity at set times. Predictive scaling forecasts load from history.

problem_ideas: An Auto Scaling group has min 2, desired 4, max 10; traffic doubles and each instance can serve 25% more: predict the new instance count.
With target tracking at 50% CPU, 4 instances average 80%: roughly how many instances will the group grow to?
A retailer knows traffic triples every Black Friday at 09:00: which scaling policy fits best?
One instance fails its health check overnight: predict the group's instance count before and after replacement.
At 03:00 the load drops to almost nothing but the group stays at 2 instances: explain why.
Compare monthly instance-hours for a fixed fleet of 10 versus an Auto Scaling group running 3 instances for 16 hours a day and 10 for 8 hours a day.
